A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, six figures, and Appendices A–I are readable and support comparison across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical simulations of weak-to-strong generalization in ReLU and linear random-feature networks, including student-width ablations in Figures 2–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and ablations in Figures 2–6 and Appendices H–I.

M1.justification: Both versions use fixed random features, a population-optimal teacher, and a zero-initialized student trained on teacher labels with early-stopped gradient flow. The broader discussion of learning rules in v2 concerns theoretical applicability rather than a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic regression settings: spherical inputs with ReLU features and anisotropic Gaussian inputs with linear features. The dimensionality and target-support sweeps in Appendix I are retained.

E2.justification: The teacher–student comparisons and student-width controls are unchanged. Newly cited methods are discussed as related work, without being added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix H and the figure captions retain the same simulation procedures, student widths, training-time sweeps, loss metrics, optimal-stopping comparisons, and log-space curve fitting. No experimental setting is substantively revised.

E4.justification: Both retain the early-stopping analyses, the 8192-versus-16384 student-width ablation in Figure 5, and the additional dimensionality and target-support analyses in Figures 4 and 6.

E5.justification: Appendix H in both versions reports five repetitions with different random seeds and 95% confidence intervals in Figures 2(a) and 3(a). No uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: The simulation curves, result entries, and findings are unchanged. Both retain the fitted relationships L_ST = 1.18 L_TE^1.85 in Figure 2 and L_ST = 1.12 L_TE^2.03 in Figure 3, together with the same appendix results.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3 changes to any fixed alpha > 0 at sufficiently large dimension; Theorem 4.3 relaxes target normalization to E[f*^2] <= 1; and Theorem D.6 adds a factor of 8 to its upper bound. Most promoted lemmas and limitation results already existed in v1. The new Lemma 6.10 also displays an eigenvalue denominator inconsistent with Appendix C.11.

C1.justification: The positive generalization claims and quadratic limitation remain. v2 broadens the abstract and introduction's explicit limitation scope to arbitrary or pretrained feature spaces and additional learning rules, although the underlying general shrinkage-optimality theorem already appeared as v1 Theorem 6.11.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the narrow random-feature caveat with a substantial account of applicability: origin-containing convex classes, origin-minimized regularizers, and the distinction between training a fresh head on pretrained features and fine-tuning a pretrained predictor. It also explains why shrinkage optimality is not transitive and why bootstrapping needs a different argument.

D1.justification: Appendix H retains the same analytical simulation description, numpy.polyfit procedure, one-H100 hardware disclosure, and completion within 24 GPU hours. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v2 removes v1's argument that several prior approaches fail to establish weak-to-strong generalization in a strict sense. It instead identifies closely related settings and explains when its lower bound applies to Charikar et al., while recasting Ildiz et al. as distillation. Historical, optimization, and empirical citations also expand the positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, mechanism explanation, and general-results narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves to Section 7, limitation results are consolidated in Section 4, and gradient-flow derivations move to Appendix A. v2 also introduces widespread incorrect 'Theorem' labels in references to models, conditions, and lemmas.

P2.justification: The same six figures retain their plots, panels, axes, and legends. Figures 2–3 are repositioned within pages, captions receive limited edits, and surrounding text and mathematical displays are reflowed. No figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing results easier to interpret through clearer organization and substantially more precise discussion of the lower bounds' applicability, especially for pretrained models. The central theory and experimental evidence remain largely unchanged. New formula inconsistencies, including Section 4's missing square and Lemma 6.10's denominator mismatch with Appendix C.11, together with misleading cross-reference labels, limit the overall gain.
